doc.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: The hardships of life on the road
summary: Wess describes the physical toll of touring, irregular meals and sleep, and says the travel is the hardest part.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: We’ve been interested in seeing if we can give some of our students an idea of what it must have been like to live on the road, and you did a couple of different periods of it.
Yeah, is it all it’s cracked up to be or is it—

It’s rough. It’s like, well in the first place it’s physical, you know? And if you’re not, if your body’s not in good shape you’re not really going to make it. Because everything is without a schedule. So you don’t eat on time, you don’t sleep on time, you don’t do anything at the same time. So it’s just that kind of life. And sometimes you have to work without sleep and food, you know. It all depends on what happens. The hardest part of it is getting to the gig. After you get there, it’s not hard to play but I mean—
Yeah, it’s the parts in between, right?
Yeah. Everything that’s involved in the transportation and the lodging and all that happens makes it difficult.
What was — relate for us maybe one of your worst experiences on the road or one of your best experiences.
Oh, I can’t. I don’t know. I really can’t remember.
